Specimen: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Fragile-X syndrome

TEST PERFORMED
FRAXA Expansion Analysis
PCR assay for CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene

RESULTS
FMR1 (FRAXA) Analysis: NORMAL

Allele 1: 30 CGG repeats
Allele 2: 31 CGG repeats

No expansion mutation detected in the FMR1 gene.

INTERPRETATION
This patient has two normal-sized FRAXA alleles. The absence of an expanded allele makes it very unlikely that this individual is affected with Fragile-X syndrome.

TECHNICAL NOTES
FRAXA Allele Size Ranges:
- Normal: 5-44 CGG repeats
- Intermediate: 45-54 CGG repeats
- Premutation: 55-200 CGG repeats
- Full mutation: >200 CGG repeats

TEST LIMITATIONS
This PCR-based assay detects CGG repeat expansions in the FMR1 gene. Approximately <1% of Fragile-X syndrome cases may be caused by point mutations, deletions, or other rearrangements within FMR1 that would not be detected by this method. If clinical suspicion remains high, additional testing such as FMR1 sequencing or deletion/duplication analysis may be considered.

SUMMARY
Normal FRAXA allele size. No expansion mutation detected in FMR1 gene. Very unlikely to be affected with Fragile-X syndrome.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
